hindi: दान का भाव, प्रिय बोलना, धीरता, उचित का ज्ञान — चार सहज गुण अभ्यास से प्राप्त नहीं किए जाते।
english: Generosity, pleasant speech, steadiness, knowledge of what is fitting: four innate virtues are not obtained by practice.
notes: sahajā for sahajāḥ is regular visarga loss before a voiced consonant, not a typo.
lines_deva: अभ्यासेन न लभ्यन्ते चत्वारः सहजा गुणाः
lines_iast: abhyāsena na labhyante catvāraḥ sahajā guṇāḥ

hindi: अपने वर्ग को छोड़कर दूसरे के वर्ग का आश्रय ले; स्वयं ही विनाश को जाता है, जैसे राजा दूसरे के धर्म से।
english: Having abandoned one's own group, one would resort to another's group; one goes to ruin by oneself indeed, as a king through another's dharma.
notes: rājānyadharmataḥ read as rājā + anya-dharmataḥ; it could also be split rāja-anya-dharmataḥ. samāśrayet is optative with no relative or conditional particle; rendered 'would' as a conditional. The subject of yāti is unstated ('one').

hindi: हाथी स्थूल शरीर वाला है और वह अंकुश के वश में है; क्या अंकुश हाथी भर है? दीपक के जलने पर अंधकार नष्ट होता है; क्या अंधकार दीपक भर है? वज्र से भी मारे गए पर्वत गिरते हैं; क्या पर्वत वज्र भर हैं? जिसका तेज शोभा देता है, वह बलवान है; स्थूलों में क्या भरोसा?
english: The elephant is of massive body, and he is under the goad's control: is the goad only the size of an elephant? When a lamp is lit, darkness vanishes: is darkness only the size of a lamp? Even struck by a thunderbolt, mountains fall: are the mountains only the size of a thunderbolt? He whose brilliance shines is strong: what trust is there in the massive?
notes: nagā- at the end of line c continues as nagāḥ with stejo (tejaḥ) in line d; the printed line break splits nagāḥ / tejaḥ. mātra rendered 'only the size of'. vajramātraṃ is neuter singular beside masculine plural nagāḥ; read as a predicate 'only the size of a thunderbolt', as in the parallel hastimātraḥ and dīpamātram.
lines_deva: हस्ती स्थूलतनुः स चाङ्कुशवशः किं हस्तिमात्रोऽङ्कुशो
दीपे प्रज्वलिते प्रणश्यति तमः किं दीपमात्रं तमः
वज्रेणापि हताः पतन्ति गिरयः किं वज्रमात्रं नगा-
स्तेजो यस्य विराजते स बलवान्स्थूलेषु कः प्रत्ययः
lines_iast: hastī sthūlatanuḥ sa cāṅkuśavaśaḥ kiṃ hastimātro'ṅkuśo
dīpe prajvalite praṇaśyati tamaḥ kiṃ dīpamātraṃ tamaḥ
vajreṇāpi hatāḥ patanti girayaḥ kiṃ vajramātraṃ nagā-
stejo yasya virājate sa balavānsthūleṣu kaḥ pratyayaḥ

hindi: कलियुग में दस हज़ार के लिए हरि पृथ्वी को छोड़ते हैं; उसका आधा, जाह्नवी का जल; उसका आधा, ग्रामदेवता।
english: In the Kali age, for ten thousand, Hari leaves the earth; half of that, the water of the Jāhnavī; half of that, the village deities.
notes: Elliptical: the second half-line has no verb; tyajati is carried over. daśasahasrāṇi is read as an accusative of duration with no unit stated (the Sanskrit gives no word for 'years'); it could also be read as the object. Jāhnavī is a river name; no identification made.

words.gloss: of one attached to the home

hindi: घर में आसक्त का विद्या नहीं, मांसभोजी का दया नहीं, द्रव्य के लोभी का सत्य नहीं, स्त्रैण का पवित्रता नहीं।
english: Of one attached to the home, no learning; of a flesh-eater, no compassion; of one greedy for riches, no truth; of one given to women, no purity.
notes: No verb in the Sanskrit; none supplied. The genitives are kept as genitives ('of one …, no …'), not 'for'. straiṇa literally 'of women', one given to women.
lines_deva: गृहासक्तस्य नो विद्या नो दया मांसभोजिनः
द्रव्यलुब्धस्य नो सत्यं स्त्रैणस्य न पवित्रता
lines_iast: gṛhāsaktasya no vidyā no dayā māṃsabhojinaḥ
dravyalubdhasya no satyaṃ straiṇasya na pavitratā

words.gram: pres. pass. part. √śikṣ, m. nom. sg.

hindi: दुर्जन अनेक प्रकार से सिखाया जाता हुआ भी साधु की दशा को नहीं पाता; दूध, घी से जड़ तक सींचा हुआ निम्ब वृक्ष मधुरता को नहीं पाता।
english: A wicked man does not attain the state of the good, even when taught in many ways; a nimba tree sprinkled to the root with milk, ghee, does not attain sweetness.
notes: Two statements side by side with no 'like'; none added. payasā ghṛtena stand without ca, rendered as a row.

words.gloss: by hundreds of baths at holy places

hindi: भीतर गए मल वाला बुरा सैकड़ों तीर्थस्नानों से भी शुद्ध नहीं होता, जैसे मदिरा का पात्र, तपाया हुआ और विद्यमान।
english: One with filth gone within, a bad one, does not become pure even by hundreds of baths at holy places, as a vessel of liquor, heated and existent.
notes: surāyā is surāyāḥ with regular visarga loss before d. 'dāhitaṃ ca sat' is rendered literally (dāhita heated, ca and, sat being); its exact sense (for instance 'though heated') is uncertain and no 'though' is added. duṣṭa rendered 'bad'.
lines_deva: न शुध्यति यथा भाण्डं सुराया दाहितं च सत्
lines_iast: na śudhyati yathā bhāṇḍaṃ surāyā dāhitaṃ ca sat

hindi: जो जिसके गुण की श्रेष्ठता को नहीं जानता, वह उसकी सदा निन्दा करता है; इसमें आश्चर्य नहीं; जैसे किरात स्त्री हाथी के मस्तक से प्राप्त मोती को छोड़कर गुञ्जा धारण करती है।
english: He who does not know the excellence of someone's virtue always reviles him; there is nothing wonderful in this; as a Kirāta woman, having abandoned the pearl got from an elephant's temple, wears a guñjā.
notes: Relative pair yaḥ ... yasya rendered with 'someone's'. kumbha is the elephant's frontal globe; 'temple' used. Kirāta is a tribal name; guñjā is the name of a seed. bibharti 'wears' (literally bears).
lines_deva: स तं सदा निन्दति नात्र चित्रम्
lines_iast: sa taṃ sadā nindati nātra citram

hindi: जो पूरे एक वर्ष तक नित्य मौन से भोजन करते हैं, उनके द्वारा हज़ार करोड़ युगों तक स्वर्गलोक में सम्मान पाया जाता है।
english: Those who always eat in silence for a full year: by them one is honoured in the heavenly world for a thousand crores of yugas.
notes: tu is printed but left untranslated as a weak connective. taiḥ is instrumental with a passive-form verb (mahīyate); rendered literally; the intended sense is probably that they themselves are honoured. koṭi = ten million.
lines_deva: ये तु संवत्सरं पूर्णं नित्यं मौनेन भुञ्जते
lines_iast: ye tu saṃvatsaraṃ pūrṇaṃ nityaṃ maunena bhuñjate

words.gloss: excess of sleep, excess of service

hindi: काम-क्रोध, तथा लोभ, मिठास-शृङ्गार-कौतुक, अति निद्रा और अति सेवा — विद्यार्थी निश्चय ही आठ का त्याग करे।
english: Desire and anger, likewise greed, sweetness, adornment, curiosity, excess of sleep and excess of service: a seeker of learning should indeed avoid eight.
notes: The eight are counted as kāma, krodha, lobha, svādu, śṛṅgāra, kautuka, ati-nidrā, ati-seva; the dual endings of -kautuke and -atiseve do not match a three-member and a two-member list, so the grouping of svādu-śṛṅgāra-kautuke is uncertain. śṛṅgāra can mean adornment or amorous sentiment; seva can mean service or indulgence.

words.gloss: delighting in living in the forest

hindi: अकृष्ट फल-मूल, सदा वनवास में रत, प्रतिदिन श्राद्ध करता है; वह ब्राह्मण ऋषि कहा जाता है।
english: Uncultivated fruits and roots, delighting always in living in the forest, he performs śrāddha day after day; that brahmin is called a sage.
notes: akṛṣṭaphalamūlāni is accusative plural; it is left bare in the translation; its relation to the śrāddha (means or offering) is not stated in the Sanskrit. The verse has no relative; subject is the brahmin of line b.

words.gloss: one who approaches at the season-time

hindi: एक आहार से सन्तुष्ट, सदा छह कर्मों में लगा हुआ और ऋतुकाल में गमन करने वाला, वह ब्राह्मण द्विज कहा जाता है।
english: Satisfied with one meal, always engaged in the six actions, and one who approaches at the season-time, that brahmin is called twice-born.
notes: The object of abhigāmī is not stated; none supplied. The six actions are not listed in the line.
lines_deva: ऋतुकालाभिगामी च स विप्रो द्विज उच्यते
lines_iast: ṛtukālābhigāmī ca sa vipro dvija ucyate

words.gloss: having trade and agriculture as action

hindi: लौकिक कर्म में रत, पशुओं का पालक, जो वाणिज्य और कृषि के कर्म वाला है, वह ब्राह्मण वैश्य कहा जाता है।
english: Engaged in worldly action, a protector of animals, he whose action is trade and agriculture, that brahmin is called a vaiśya.
notes: Hindi 'और' joins vāṇijya and kṛṣi inside the compound.
lines_deva: वाणिज्यकृषिकर्मा यः स विप्रो वैश्य उच्यते
lines_iast: vāṇijyakṛṣikarmā yaḥ sa vipro vaiśya ucyate

words.gloss: of lac and the like, oil, indigo

hindi: लाख आदि, तेल, नील, कौसुम्भ, मधु, घी, मद्य, मांस का विक्रेता, वह ब्राह्मण शूद्र कहा जाता है।
english: A seller of lac and the like, oil, indigo, kausumbha, honey, ghee, liquor, meat: that brahmin is called a śūdra.
notes: kausumbha kept as the name of a commodity; no identification made. The genitive list has no ca.
lines_deva: विक्रेता मद्यमांसानां स विप्रः शूद्र उच्यते
lines_iast: vikretā madyamāṃsānāṃ sa vipraḥ śūdra ucyate

hindi: दूसरों के कार्य का नाशक और दम्भी, अपना स्वार्थ साधने वाला, छली, द्वेषी, मृदु, क्रूर, ब्राह्मण बिलाव कहा जाता है।
english: A destroyer of others' work and a hypocrite, an accomplisher of his own ends, deceitful, malicious, soft, cruel: a brahmin is called a cat.
notes: dāmbhika is one who practises dambha (ostentation, hypocrisy).
lines_deva: छली द्वेषी मृदुः क्रूरो विप्रो मार्जार उच्यते
lines_iast: chalī dveṣī mṛduḥ krūro vipro mārjāra ucyate

hindi: बावड़ी, कुआँ, तालाब, उद्यान, देवालयों के उच्छेदन में निर्भय, वह ब्राह्मण म्लेच्छ कहा जाता है।
english: Fearless in destroying stepwells, wells, tanks, gardens, abodes of gods, that brahmin is called a mleccha.
notes: vāpī rendered 'stepwell' (a pool or well with steps); sura-veśman literally 'abode of gods'. The genitive plural depends on ucchedane.
lines_deva: उच्छेदने निराशङ्कः स विप्रो म्लेच्छ उच्यते
lines_iast: ucchedane nirāśaṅkaḥ sa vipro mleccha ucyate

hindi: देवता का धन, गुरु का धन, दूसरे की पत्नी का स्पर्श, सब प्राणियों में निर्वाह, ब्राह्मण चाण्डाल कहा जाता है।
english: Wealth of the gods, wealth of the teacher, touching another's wife, maintenance among all beings: a brahmin is called a caṇḍāla.
notes: The first half-line is a bare list of nominatives with no verb or participle; the sense of nirvāhaḥ sarvabhūteṣu (maintenance, livelihood or carrying on among all beings) is uncertain and is rendered literally.

words.gloss: devoid of giving and enjoying of honey

hindi: पुण्यवानों द्वारा धन, भोग के लिए धन, दिया जाना चाहिए; उसका संचय निश्चय ही नहीं। श्रीकर्ण का और बलि का, पराक्रम के स्वामी का, यश आज भी स्थित है। हमारा मधु के दान और भोग से रहित, चिरकाल से संचित स्वामी; निर्वाण से ऐसा, अपने पैरों का जोड़ा मक्खियाँ रगड़ती हैं, अहो।
english: Wealth, wealth for enjoying, is to be given by the meritorious; no hoarding of it indeed. Even today the fame of Śrī-Karṇa and of Bali, of the lord of valour, stands. Our lord, devoid of giving and enjoying of honey, long hoarded: from extinction, thus, the bees rub their own pair of feet, ah.

text_flags.why: possible: the root √dhṛṣ does not give a form dharṣanti, while √ghṛṣ 'rub' gives gharṣanti and suits pāda-yugalam as object.

possible: 'lord' gives no clear sense as the object of saṃcitam in a line about hoarded honey; the form nātham is kept as printed. Alternative on sense and agreement only: naṣṭaṃ 'lost' (no source in hand); a guess for a human to settle.

notes: Translation of lines c and d is tentative: the syntax of asmākaṃ ... nāthaṃ cirāt saṃcitaṃ ... iti is unclear, the two flagged forms are doubtful, and nirvāṇāt 'from extinction' is kept literal. makṣikā can also mean flies. śrīkarṇasya may be a single name or Śrī (honorific) with Karṇa; vikramapateḥ is read as 'lord of valour' and could be a name or an epithet. In line a, bhojyadhanaṃ dhanaṃ is rendered as two appositive words. The comma before 'of the lord of valour' follows the Sanskrit order only; vikramapateḥ after baleś ca could be a third person rather than an epithet of Bali.
lines_deva: देयं भोज्यधनं धनं सुकृतिभिर्नो सञ्चयस्तस्य वै
lines_iast: deyaṃ bhojyadhanaṃ dhanaṃ sukṛtibhirno sañcayastasya vai
